text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes treatment focuses on lowering blood sugar, managing weight, and preventing organ or heart damage. Doctors use a step-by-step approach that combines healthy habits, oral or injectable medications, and sometimes surgery.

list.snippet: Healthy Eating: Choose non-starchy vegetables, lean proteins, and complex carbohydrates while cutting back on added sugars and refined grains.
Physical Activity: Incorporating regular moderate-to-vigorous exercise (such as brisk walking) plus muscle-strengthening sessions supports overall metabolic health.
Weight Management: Losing a modest percentage of your body weight can improve how your body uses insulin and help lower blood pressure and cholesterol.

text_blocks.snippet: If diet and exercise are not enough, doctors usually prescribe pills first. Many people take a combination of these drugs:

list.snippet: Metformin (Biguanide): This is almost always the first-line medication. It lowers how much glucose your liver makes and helps your cells respond better to insulin.
Sulfonylureas: Medications like glipizide and glimepiride make the pancreas release more insulin.
SGLT2 Inhibitors: These pills help your kidneys remove extra sugar through your urine, and they can also protect your heart and kidneys.
DPP-4 Inhibitors (Gliptins): These help block digestive enzymes to keep blood sugar from spiking after meals.
Thiazolidinediones (TZDs): Drugs like pioglitazone make muscle and fat cells more sensitive to insulin.
Meglitinides: Fast-acting pills taken around meal times to trigger a quick release of insulin.

GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Injectable drugs (such as semaglutide or liraglutide) slow down digestion, help you feel full, encourage your pancreas to release insulin when needed, and often assist with weight loss.
Dual GLP-1/GIP Agonists: Newer combination injectables that provide even stronger blood sugar and weight management.

If your pancreas eventually produces very little insulin, or if other medications do not keep your numbers in range, your doctor may prescribe insulin injections (long-acting, short-acting, or a mix) or an insulin pump.
Weight Loss (Bariatric) Surgery: Recommended for individuals with severe obesity, this surgery can dramatically improve blood sugar control and sometimes put type 2 diabetes into remission.
